subject: Cooking
title: Organic Food Isn't Necessarily Healthier
description: A micro-lesson that makes Organic Food Isn't Necessarily Healthier usable.

hook.text: Organic food costs 20–100% more. Consumers believe it's healthier. The evidence is surprisingly thin.

buildup.text: Organic farming restricts synthetic pesticides and fertilizers but allows 'natural' ones — some equally toxic.

discovery.text: Stanford's 2012 meta-analysis found no significant nutritional difference between organic and conventional produce.

twist.text: Organic farming does benefit soil health, biodiversity, and reduces farmworker pesticide exposure.

climax.text: The health premium of organic is environmental, not nutritional. Both are important — but they're not the same.

punchline.text: Organic is better for the planet. Not necessarily for your body.

quiz.question: What did Stanford's 2012 meta-analysis find about organic vs. conventional food?

details.summary: Organic produce contains similar nutrient levels as conventionally grown food according to comprehensive meta-analyses. Organic farming uses different pesticides, not zero pesticides. The choice between organic and conventional is more about environmental practices than individual nutrition.
details.whyItMatters: The organic premium leads many families to spend more on groceries believing it is essential for health. Understanding the evidence allows informed spending decisions focused on eating more produce overall.
takeaways: Nutrient content is similar between organic and conventional produce
Organic farming uses approved pesticides, not zero chemicals
The biggest health benefit comes from eating more produce, period

faq.question: What do major studies say about organic nutrition?
faq.answer: A 2012 Stanford meta-analysis of 237 studies found no strong evidence that organic foods are significantly more nutritious. A 2014 British Journal of Nutrition review found slightly higher antioxidant levels in organic crops, but the health significance of that difference is uncertain.

faq.question: Are there any benefits to buying organic?
faq.answer: Organic farming practices generally have lower environmental impact through reduced synthetic chemical use. Organic produce has lower pesticide residues, though conventional levels are also within safety limits.
